result:
I graded s2 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`: three items correct, two partial and one wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only outputs a tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You picked "it will eventually fix the bug". After 40 identical failures more steps add nothing, so the loop needs a step limit that stops it and reports back. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is the right count. But your reason says the model runs the tools itself. The program runs them, and the model makes one call per input it receives. |
| q5 | correct | You gave both the what and the why, and the group-chat comparison fits. |
| q6 | partial | The name is only part of it. The model chooses from each tool's full description: what it does and the parameters it takes. |

**What you have down:** the structure of the loop, what the model outputs when it wants a tool, and why results go back in as the next input.

**What to fix:**
- **Who runs tools:** the model only requests them, and your program runs them.
- **Stopping condition:** an agent needs one, such as a step limit.
- **Tool descriptions:** the model relies on the whole description, not just the name.

**Next step:** write a one-sentence description for `check_calendar` that says what it does and what each argument means. After that we move on to context and memory.

I also added learning record `0003-loop-recall-and-open-gaps.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded.
